AppValidation validates the app metadata based on the OS and other parameters

- This function validates the app based on the metadata

--------------------------------------------------------------------
ANDROID

 1. Lambda OS Version is not a regex and is not empty
    a. Check if the app supports the OS version passed by the user (min and max version)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
IOS

 1. Simulator apps are not supported on real device
 2. Certificate expiry for app in case of resign app false
 3. App Store signing type requires resignApp to be true
 4. Lambda OS Version is not a regex and is not empty
    a. Check if the app supports the OS version passed by the user (min version) also check for minor versions
    b. Public cloud, Resign app false, iOS18 in public enterprise app not supported
 5. Check if the device name is supported by the app
    a. Check if app supports iphone or ipad or both

functions.name: updateClassByBuildID

It fetches all active classes for the given build and updates each one individually.

  - buildId: The ID of the build whose classes need to be updated
  - orgId: The organization ID for permission context
  - userId: The user ID for permission context

functions.name: updateClass
functions.signature: (*frameworkTestManager) updateClass(classId int, org_id int, user_id int)
functions.description:
updateClass updates the status of a class based on the status of its tests
It calculates the appropriate status for the class and updates the database accordingly
It also sends SSE notifications when the class status changes to running or an end state

Parameters:
  - classId: The ID of the class to update
  - org_id: The organization ID for permission context
  - user_id: The user ID for permission context

functions.name: updateFrameworkBuild
functions.signature: (*frameworkTestManager) updateFrameworkBuild(buildId int, isExpire bool, expireStatus string, expireRemark string, shardId string, contextLogger *logrus.Entry)
functions.description:
updateFrameworkBuild updates the status of a build based on the status of its classes or shards.
It calculates the appropriate status for the build and updates the database accordingly.
It also sends SSE notifications when the build status changes to running or an end state.

Parameters:
- buildId: The ID of the build to update
- isExpire: Flag indicating if this is an expiration update (timeout, error, etc.)
- expireStatus: The status to set if isExpire is true
- expireRemark: Additional remarks to include if isExpire is true
- shardId: The ID of the shard if applicable (empty string if not shard-based)
- contextLogger: Logger with context for consistent logging

The function handles errors during database operations and logs them appropriately.

functions.name: updateTestByShardId
functions.signature: (*frameworkTestManager) updateTestByShardId(shardId string, reqStatus string, testRemark string, orgId int, userId int, contextLogger *logrus.Entry)
functions.description:
updateTestByShardId updates the status of all tests for a given shard
It handles different status transitions based on the requested status and current test status
Parameters:
- shardId: The ID of the shard whose tests need to be updated
- reqStatus: The requested status to update tests to (e.g., timeout, error)
- testRemark: Additional remarks to be stored with the test update
- orgId: Organization ID for SSE event
- userId: User ID for SSE event
- contextLogger: Logger for tracking execution

functions.name: updateShardByBuildID
functions.description:
updateShardByBuildID updates the status of all shards associated with a specific build ID.
It fetches all active shards for the given build and updates each one individually.

Parameters:
  - shardPayload: Contains build ID, job ID, shard status, org ID, user ID, and remarks
  - contextLogger: Logger for tracking execution flow

functions.name: updateClassByShardId
functions.signature: (*frameworkTestManager) updateClassByShardId(shardId string, orgId int, userId int, contextLogger *logrus.Entry)
functions.description:
updateClassByShardId updates the status of all classes associated with a specific shard.
It fetches all classes for the given shard ID that are not in an inactive or end state,
then calls UpdateClass for each class to update its status based on its tests.

Parameters:
- shardId: The ID of the shard whose classes need to be updated
- orgId: Organization ID for the classes
- userId: User ID for tracking who initiated the update
- contextLogger: Logger with context for consistent logging

The function handles errors during database operations and logs them appropriately.
SSE (Server-Sent Events) for UI updates are handled inside the UpdateClass function.

functions.name: updateShard
functions.signature: (*frameworkTestManager) updateShard(job_id string, buildId int, shardId string, reqStatus string, org_id int, user_id int, group_id int, testId string, adbEspressoSupport bool, isVirtualDevice bool, shardRemark string) string
functions.description:
updateShard updates the status of a specific shard based on the status of its classes.
It calculates the appropriate status by aggregating class statuses, updates the shard record
in the database, and sends notifications to relevant systems.

Parameters:
  - job_id: The job identifier associated with this shard
  - buildId: The build ID this shard belongs to
  - shardId: The unique identifier for the shard
  - reqStatus: Requested status to set (used when no tests exist but shard needs status update)
  - org_id: Organization ID for permission context
  - user_id: User ID for permission context
  - group_id: Group ID for permission context
  - testId: Test identifier (if applicable)
  - adbEspressoSupport: Flag indicating if ADB Espresso support is enabled
  - isVirtualDevice: Flag indicating if this is a virtual device test
  - shardRemark: Additional remarks to store with the shard

Returns:
  - newstatus: The updated status of the shard after processing

architecture.overview: Repository with 262 files across 90 modules. 1715 public exports, 433 types, 1000 functions.

ai_analysis.pattern: Layered microservice architecture with domain-driven design elements

layers.name: Presentation Layer
layers.purpose: Handle HTTP requests, WebSocket connections, and API endpoints

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.purpose: Business logic orchestration and application services

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.purpose: Core business entities and domain-specific logic

layers.name: Infrastructure Layer
layers.purpose: External integrations, persistence, and technical concerns

ai_analysis.data_flow: Requests enter through HTTP endpoints, flow through middleware for authentication/validation, reach service layer for business logic processing, interact with domain models, and persist data through repositories to database/cache. Async communication handled via Kafka producers/consumers.
strengths: Clear separation of concerns with distinct layers
Robust external integrations (Kafka, Redis, multiple databases)
Feature flag support for gradual rollouts
Proper error handling and logging mechanisms
weaknesses: High module coupling with overlapping responsibilities
Duplicate module names suggest unclear boundaries
Large number of modules may indicate over-engineering
Mixed abstraction levels in module organization
recommendations: Consolidate duplicate modules and clarify domain boundaries
Implement dependency injection to reduce coupling
Consider extracting some modules into separate microservices
Implement proper module versioning and API contracts
Add architectural decision records (ADRs) for design decisions

ai_summary.overview: A Go-based mobile management service for LambdaTest that handles mobile device testing infrastructure, including test execution, reporting, and device management. The service provides APIs for managing mobile testing sessions, build reports, analytics, and various testing frameworks like Appium.
ai_summary.purpose: To provide a comprehensive backend service for managing mobile testing operations, handling test execution lifecycle, device provisioning, reporting, and integration with various testing frameworks and external services
key_features: Mobile test session management and execution
Build and test reporting with analytics
Apple Pay card integration for testing
ai_summary.architecture_style: Microservices with layered architecture (service layer, repository layer, transport layer)
suggestions: Consider implementing OpenAPI/Swagger documentation for better API documentation
Add more comprehensive integration tests given the microservices architecture
Implement circuit breaker patterns for external service calls
Consider adding distributed tracing for better observability across services
